name: Recovery Record
one_liner: Free app for logging meals, thoughts and feelings during eating disorder recovery, which can link to your therapist or dietitian.
best_for: People in treatment for anorexia, bulimia, binge eating disorder or ARFID who want to log meals between appointments
Sharing meal and mood logs with a dietitian or therapist who uses the clinician app
Self-monitoring with coping reminders when you don't yet have a treatment team
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
Anyone with medical warning signs (fainting, chest pain, very low weight) who needs urgent medical care
People who find calorie or meal logging makes their symptoms worse
short_description: Free eating disorder self-monitoring app: log meals and the feelings around them, get coping prompts, and share logs with your treatment team.
long_description: Recovery Record is a self-monitoring app for people recovering from eating disorders, made by Recovery Record, Inc. You record meals, thoughts, feelings and behaviours, follow a meal plan, use coping tactics and view progress charts; the company recommends linking with an eating disorder specialist, who can follow your logs through a separate clinician app. The App Store listing shows it as free. In the US the company says it follows the HIPAA privacy rule, and you can delete your logs or your whole account in the app. A 2019 randomized trial of 3,294 users compared a tailored version of the app with the standard self-monitoring version; the main outcome did not differ between groups, though remission at 8 weeks was higher with the tailored version. It is a support tool, not a substitute for medical care.
patient_summary: You log meals and the thoughts and feelings around them, follow a meal plan and coping strategies, and see your progress over time. If your therapist or dietitian uses Recovery Record for Clinicians, you can link so they see your logs and send feedback. The app is free to download.

pricing.notes: Free to download on the App Store; no paid tier was listed.

privacy.notes: Says it follows the HIPAA privacy rule for US users and lets you delete your account in the app; the App Store label lists no tracking, but we could not confirm from the policy whether data is shared for ads.

seo.title: Recovery Record: Review & Pricing
seo.meta_description: Recovery Record is a free eating disorder recovery app for logging meals, thoughts and feelings, which can link to your treatment team.

faqs.q: How much does Recovery Record cost?
faqs.a: Free. Prices were checked in October 2026 and can change, so confirm with Recovery Record before you sign up.

faqs.q: Can Recovery Record replace therapy or treatment?
faqs.a: No. Recovery Record is a self-help tool that can support your wellbeing or work alongside therapy, but it doesn't diagnose or treat conditions. If you're in crisis, call or text 988 in the US.

faqs.q: Where can I use Recovery Record?
faqs.a: Recovery Record is available on iPhone and Android.
Meal, thought and feeling logs; Meal plans and coping tactics; Progress charts; Link with your treatment team.

clinical_trials.study: Randomized trial of a tailored versus standard version of Recovery Record

citation.authors: Tregarthen J, Paik Kim J, Sadeh-Sharvit S, Neri E, Welch H, Lock J
citation.title: Comparing a Tailored Self-Help Mobile App With a Standard Self-Monitoring App for the Treatment of Eating Disorder Symptoms: Randomized Controlled Trial

clinical_trials.outcome: No difference between the tailored and standard app on the main outcome (clinically meaningful EDE-Q change); remission at 8 weeks was higher with the tailored version (53.3% vs 31.1%).
clinical_trials.study_design: Randomized controlled trial comparing two versions of the app (no non-app control)

primary_uses: Sharing logs with your treatment team
